documents.title: Optional Guidelines for AI Use in Courses
documents.stance_why: The page says faculty 'may select from among four different permission levels' and that the guidelines 'do not constitute official university policy'. It sets no single rule and hands the choice to instructors, so delegates, with the four options listed as tiers.
documents.summary: Provost-hosted optional guidelines giving instructors a four-level menu of AI permissions with ready-to-paste syllabus language, a menu of allowable-use categories, a list of unacceptable uses and a required AI Contributions disclosure. It states it is guidelines only, not official policy.

units.why: The page calls itself a shared vocabulary for AI use in 'any course context' and links to the Academic Integrity Policy; this sets scope and purpose, so it is an institution-level framework (P56) addressed to all, informing rather than commanding.

documents.stance_why: The page offers example statements and says 'Feel free to use all or parts'; the AI statement is a sample whose permissions are for 'this course'. It sets no university-wide AI stance, so delegates.
documents.summary: Example academic-integrity statements for syllabi. Two mention AI: unauthorized AI use is an integrity violation, and a sample course statement permits AI for brainstorming and grammar checking while treating AI content presented as original as unauthorized.

units.why: 'All work submitted in this course must be your own' in the example integrity statement: P29.
units.anchor: All work submitted in this course must be your own.
units.frag_start: All Auburn University students are expected to act with honesty

units.why: 'This includes the unauthorized use of AI' lists unauthorized AI use among violations of the Academic Integrity Policy: P36.
units.anchor: This includes the unauthorized use of AI.
units.frag_start: Violations of the Auburn University Academic Integrity Policy

units.why: 'All instances of alleged violations ... will be reported to the Office of the Provost for review and appropriate action' sets the route for handling violations; this is an integrity process, P36.
units.anchor: will be reported to the Office of the Provost for review and appropriate action
units.frag_start: All instances of alleged violations of the Academic Integrity Policy

units.why: 'Unauthorized use of AI is included in violations of the Academic Integrity Policy': P36.
units.anchor: Unauthorized use of AI is included in violations of the Academic Integrity Policy.
units.frag_start: Unauthorized use of AI is included

units.why: 'for this course, students are allowed to use AI to brainstorm ideas or check grammar' is a sample narrow permission: P15 (brainstorming) is the closest single type; grammar checking is P18 but the listed pair is one rule.
units.anchor: students are allowed to use AI to brainstorm ideas or check grammar
units.frag_start: for this course, students are allowed to use AI

units.why: 'Presenting content generated through AI as original work is considered unauthorized use of AI': P19.
units.anchor: Presenting content generated through AI as original work is considered unauthorized use of AI.
units.frag_start: Presenting content generated through AI

units.why: The page tells faculty that course-specific violations 'should be added' to the syllabus integrity statement; it puts expectations in the syllabus: P09.
units.anchor: If there are violations that are specific to your course, those violations should be added
units.frag_start: If there are violations that are specific
units.policy: If there are violations specific to a course, those violations should be added to the Academic Integrity statement in the syllabus.

notes: Coder A. No school or computing policy found per collect file; course layer deferred. The Provost guidelines and the Biggio page repeat the same four options; each document was coded on its own. P04 used where the sentence is about who decides, P05 for named-level menus.
